arxiv-2104-00723.title: Andreev interference in the surface accumulation layer of half-shell InAsSb/Al hybrid nanowires
arxiv-2104-00723.creator: Lukas Stampfer, Damon J. Carrad, Dags Olsteins, Christian E. N. Petersen, Sabbir A. Khan, Peter Krogstrup, Thomas S. Jespersen
arxiv-2104-00723.description: Abstract Understanding the spatial distribution of charge carriers in III-V nanowires proximity coupled to superconductors is important for the design and interpretation of experiments based on hybrid quantum devices. In this letter, the gate-dependent surface accumulation layer of InAsSb/Al nanowires was studied by means of Andreev interference in a parallel magnetic field.

arxiv-2106-01241.title: Stochastic maximum principle for systems driven by local martingales with spatial parameters
arxiv-2106-01241.creator: Jian Song label=e2]txjsong@sdu.edu.cn, Meng Wanglabel=e3]wangmeng22@mail.sdu.edu.cn
arxiv-2106-01241.description: Abstract We consider the stochastic optimal control problem for the dynamical system of the stochastic differential equation driven by a local martingale with a spatial parameter. Assuming the convexity of the control domain, we obtain the stochastic maximum principle as the necessary condition for an optimal control, and we also prove its sufficiency under proper conditions.

arxiv-2306-03151.title: DISCount : Counting in Large Image Collections with Detector-Based Importance Sampling
arxiv-2306-03151.creator: Gustavo Perez Subhransu Maji Daniel SheldonManning College of Information & Computer SciencesUniversity of Massachusetts, Amherst {gperezsarabi, smaji, sheldon}@cs.umass.edu
arxiv-2306-03151.description: Abstract Many modern applications use computer vision to detect and count objects in massive image collections. However, when the detection task is very difficult or in the presence of domain shifts, the counts may be inaccurate even with significant investments in training data and model development.

arxiv-2402-01925.description: Abstract . arxiv-2409-15354.title: An Informatics Framework for the Design of Sustainable, Chemically Recyclable, Synthetically-Accessible and Durable Polymers
arxiv-2409-15354.creator: Joseph Kern, Yongliang Su, Will Gutekunst, Rampi Ramprasad
arxiv-2409-15354.description: Abstract We present a novel approach to design durable and chemically recyclable ring-opening polymerization (ROP) class polymers. This approach employs digital reactions using virtual forward synthesis (VFS) to generate over 7 million ROP polymers and machine learning techniques to rapidly predict thermal, thermodynamic and mechanical properties crucial for application-specific performance and recyclability.

arxiv-2412-10883.title: Hyperuniformity scaling of maximally random jammed packings of two-dimensional binary disks
arxiv-2412-10883.creator: Charles Emmett Maher, Salvatore Torquato
arxiv-2412-10883.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Charles Emmett Maher, Salvatore Torquato. Jammed (mechanically rigid) polydisperse circular-disk packings in two dimensions (2D) are popular models for structural glass formers. Maximally random jammed (MRJ) states, which are the most disordered packings subject to strict jamming, have been shown to be hyperuniform. The characterization of the hyperuniformity of MRJ circular-disk packings has covered only a very small part of the possible parameter space for the disk-size distributions.

arxiv-2507-00764.title: Insight into the combustion dynamics of ITA-driven swirl flames Journal: Combustion and Flame
arxiv-2507-00764.creator: SK Thirumalaikumaran, Balasundaram Mohan, Saptarshi Basu
arxiv-2507-00764.description: Abstract In this article, we examine the flame, flow, and acoustic coupling of Intrinsic ThermoAcoustic (ITA) driven combustion instability using a high-shear swirl injector in a model combustor. The combustor is operated using pure methane and methane-hydrogen mixture as fuels with air in a partially premixed mode.

arxiv-2510-19281.title: An Empirical Study of Bitwise Operators Intuitiveness through Performance Metrics CCS: Human-centered computing Empirical studies in HCI

arxiv-2510-19281.description: Abstract . arxiv-2601-02594.title: Annealed Langevin Posterior Sampling (ALPS): A Rapid Algorithm for Image Restoration with Multiscale Energy Models
arxiv-2601-02594.creator: Jyothi Rikhab Chand, Mathews Jacob
arxiv-2601-02594.description: Abstract Solving inverse problems in imaging requires models that support efficient inference, uncertainty quantification, and principled probabilistic reasoning. Energy-Based Models (EBMs), with their interpretable energy landscapes and compositional structure, are well-suited for this task but have historically suffered from high computational costs and training instability.

pmc-11481658.title: Pyroptosis-related genes features on prediction of the prognosis in liver cancer: An integrated analysis of bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing
pmc-11481658.creator: Zhihao Zhang, Feng Liu, Xin Lan, Fuhai Wang, Jiahao Sun, Honglong Wei
pmc-11481658.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). ObjectiveThis study explores the impact of pyroptosis-related genes (PRG) on the prognosis of liver cancer (LC).Methods421 samples (371 tumor samples and 50 normal samples) from the Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) were included in this study. GSE14520 dataset (data of RNA expression and relevant clinicopathological features), GSE125449 dataset (single-cell data in LC) and HCCDB18 dataset (validation on the reliability of the model) were downloaded as appropriate. Download the PRG and its corresponding pathway information from the gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) website.

pmc-12583421.title: Tree Height and the Asymptotic Mean of the Colijn–Plazzotta Rank of Unlabeled Binary Rooted Trees
pmc-12583421.creator: Luc Devroye, Michael R Doboli, Noah A Rosenberg, Stephan Wagner
pmc-12583421.description: The Colijn–Plazzotta ranking is a bijective encoding of the unlabeled binary rooted trees with positive integers. We show that the rank f(t) of a tree t is closely related to its height h, the maximal path length from a leaf to the root.

pmc-12964123.title: Scenario-aware control of multipathway spread processes: Application to biological invasions
pmc-12964123.creator: Prathyush Sambaturu, Manisha Sudhir, Hongze Chen, Anil Vullikanti, Rangaswamy Muniappan, Abhijin Adiga, Derek Abbott
pmc-12964123.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Optimal control of spread processes over networks is a challenging problem, even for simple diffusion models. Real-world processes—such as infectious disease outbreaks and biological invasions—often involve multiple spread pathways and time-varying network dynamics.

pmc-13023674.title: From Selection to Use: Aptamers as Targeting Reagents in Hematology
pmc-13023674.creator: Brandon Albert, Fiona Ebanks, Kimia Gharagozloo, Xinying Hai, Raymond Ngu, Sietse Munting, Maureen McKeague
pmc-13023674.description: Aptamers are synthetic nucleic acid ligands that have been proposed as alternatives to antibodies for targeting molecules and cells. In hematology, most reviews have organized aptamer literature around diseases or technological platforms. This framing has obscured how unevenly different blood cell types have been covered. In this review, we present developed aptamers organized by blood cell lineages.

pmc-13385983.title: A Culturally Embedded and Family-Oriented Approach to Thalassemia Prevention through Multisectoral Community Nursing Collaboration
pmc-13385983.creator: Henri Setiawan, Irpan Ali Rahman, Yudisa Diaz Lutfi Sandi
pmc-13385983.description: lood transfusions and iron chelation therapy, which impose significant physical, emotional, and economic burdens. Because thalassemia is inherited within families, prevention must adopt a family-oriented approach that recognizes families as the primary unit for genetic risk identification, counseling, and reproductive decision-making. Community nurses play an essential role in educating families, facilitating premarital screening, and supporting informed reproductive choices.

pmc-13583451.title: ZTTK Syndrome Expanding the Cardiac Phenotype: A Case of Shone’s Complex With a Novel SON Variant and Focused Review of the Cardiac Manifestations in ZTTK Syndrome
pmc-13583451.creator: John Coleman, Abdul L Shakerdi, Veronika Dvorakova, Janna Kenny, Abdullah Sezer
pmc-13583451.description: Zhu–Tokita–Takenouchi–Kim (ZTTK) syndrome is a rare multisystem neurodevelopmental disorder caused by heterozygous variants in SON. Presented here is a case of a four‐year‐old female with multiple rare manifestations including a complex neurodevelopmental disorder, Shone complex and a simple capillary malformation. Genetic analysis confirmed a novel frameshift variant in SON, which was classified as pathogenic.

pmc-13605298.title: AI-Powered Marine Drug Discovery: A Putative Dual c-Met/VEGFR2 Lead Candidate for Hepatocellular Carcinoma via Deep Learning and Multiscale Simulation
pmc-13605298.creator: Ruiqi Zhao, Yuhan Wang, Mengyao Han, Jiesheng Guo, Hui Hu, Shiqi Tang, Mengqing Ma, Xiaozhou Zhou, Jialing Sun
pmc-13605298.description: Background: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer mortality. The c-Met and VEGFR2 pathways synergistically drive HCC progression. Marine natural products offer chemically diverse drug reservoirs; however, conventional activity-guided isolation faces labor intensity, low throughput, and frequent compound rediscovery, limiting marine drug development.

pmc-13608253.title: From Evidence to Action: Implementing Evidence-Based Interventions for Youth Substance Use Prevention Through Drug-Free Communities and CDC's ENGAGE Framework
pmc-13608253.creator: Douglas R. Roehler, Karrie R. Thompson, Emily Rayburn, Gregory Smith, Julie Guarnizo, Ilenia Morales
pmc-13608253.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Context:Youth substance use continues to be a persistent public health concern in the United States, worsened by an evolving substance landscape that includes high-potency cannabis, nicotine vaping devices, and exposure to multiple substances. Although substantial evidence supports the effectiveness of evidence-based interventions (EBIs) for preventing youth substance use, many communities encounter difficulties in translating prevention science into coordinated and sustainable practices.Program:The Drug-Free Communities (DFC) Support Program provides critical infrastructure for coalition-based prevention efforts but does not mandate specific interventions.
